copy.bis: Kasagaran makita ang Brahminy kite sa baybayon, suba, ug kabakawanan — maayong dapit sa pagpangayam og mananap sa tubig.

copy.en: Scientists use what they know about brain signals to build advanced prosthetics — artificial arms and hands that read signals from the brain or muscles, so a person can move them just by thinking!
copy.tl: Ginagamit ng mga siyentipiko ang kaalaman sa signals ng utak para gumawa ng makabagong prosthetic — artipisyal na braso o kamay na nakababasa ng signals mula sa utak o kalamnan, kaya nagagalaw ito ng tao sa pamamagitan lang ng pag-iisip!
copy.bis: Gigamit sa mga siyentista ang ilang nahibaloan bahin sa signals sa utok aron makahimo og abante nga prosthetics — artipisyal nga bukton o kamot nga makabasa og signals gikan sa utok o kaunoran, mao nga malihok kini sa tawo pinaagi lang sa paghunahuna!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brain coral has winding ridges and grooves on its surface that together look just like a human brain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs

copy.en:
Why is it called brain coral?

Brain coral has winding ridges and grooves on its surface that together look just like a human brain — that's how it got its name.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinawag itong brain coral?

Ang brain coral ay may mga kulot na linya sa ibabaw nito na magkakasamang kamukha ng ibabaw ng utak ng tao — kaya iyon ang pangalan nito.
copy.bis:
Ngano gitawag kining brain coral?

Ang brain coral adunay liko-liko nga mga tubo ug kinhason sa ibabaw niini nga nagkasamang morag utok sa tawo — mao nga mao ang iyang ngalan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the skull (part of the skeletal system) but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. The focus is brain composition, not system function.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the brain as soft, which is a physical property, but the competency is about solid materials like hard, shiny, or stretchable. The brain is not a solid material in the intended sense, and the card does not teach properties of solid materials.

copy.en:
What is the brain actually made of?

Mostly water and fat! That's why it's soft, and why it needs the hard skull to protect it and clean fluid inside to float in.
copy.tl:
Sa ano ba talaga gawa ang utak?

Karamihan ay tubig at taba! Kaya ito malambot, at kailangan ng matigas na bungo para protektahan ito at malinis na likido para lumutang ito sa loob.
copy.bis:
Unsa ba diay ang gama sa utok?

Kasagaran tubig ug tambok! Mao nga kini humok, ug nagkinahanglan sa gahi nga bungo aron mapanalipdan ug limpyo nga likido aron maglutaw kini sa sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: blood pressure
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the brainstem controls blood pressure, which is one of the indicators of homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or explain its indicators. It only mentions a single vital function without connecting it to the concept of homeostasis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The brainstem automatically controls vital body functions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the brainstem controls vital functions, but it does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together. It does not address the interaction of body systems such as digestion and excretion, only a single organ's control of vital functions.

copy.en: The brainstem automatically controls vital body functions like breathing, your heartbeat, and blood pressure -- all without you ever thinking about it.
copy.tl: Ang brainstem ay awtomatikong nagkokontrol ng mahahalagang gawain ng katawan tulad ng paghinga, tibok ng puso, at presyon ng dugo -- kahit hindi mo ito iniisip.
copy.bis: Ang brainstem awtomatikong nagkontrol sa mahinungdanong pag-andar sa lawas sama sa paghinga, tibok sa kasingkasing, ug presyon sa dugo -- bisan wala nimo kini hunahunaa.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes brass as a mixture of copper and zinc, but it does not classify it as uniform or non-uniform, nor does it discuss solutions or suspensions. copy.en:
Did you know copper and zinc make a shiny gold-like metal?

When mixed, they form brass! Brass has a beautiful gold-like shine and is perfect for making musical instruments.
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba na ang tanso at zinc ay gumagawa ng metal na kasingkinang ng ginto?

Kapag hinaluan, nabubuo ang brass! May magandang kulay-gintong kinang ito at perpekto para sa mga instrumentong tugtugin.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang tumbaga ug zinc naghimo og metal nga kasingkidlap sa bulawan?

Kung sagolan, mahimong brass kini! Aduna kini nindong bulawanon nga kidlap ug perpekto para sa mga instrumentong tugtugon.

copy.en: After it's born, a newborn drinks its mother's milk, which gives it nutrients and protection from sickness!
copy.tl: Matapos isilang, umiinom ang sanggol ng gatas ng ina na nagbibigay ng sustansya at proteksiyon laban sa sakit!
copy.bis: Human matawo, moinom ang bata sa gatas sa inahan nga naghatag og sustansya ug panalipod batok sa sakit!

copy.en:
What gas does our body need when we breathe in?

When we breathe in, the gas our body really needs is oxygen!
copy.tl:
Anong gas ang kailangan ng ating katawan kapag humihinga tayo papasok?

Kapag humihinga tayo papasok, ang gas na kailangan ng ating katawan ay oxygen!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga gas ang gikinahanglan sa atong lawas kung mosulod ang atong ginhawa?

Kung mosulod ang atong ginhawa, ang gas nga gikinahanglan sa atong lawas mao ang oxygen!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the gas we release from our body is carbon dioxide
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card states only that exhaled gas is carbon dioxide. This single fact is a fragment of the competency's content, not direct instructional support for describing the processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the gas we release from our body is carbon dioxide

copy.en: When we breathe out, the gas we release from our body is carbon dioxide!
copy.tl: Kapag humihinga tayo palabas, ang gas na inilalabas natin mula sa katawan ay carbon dioxide!
copy.bis: Kung mogawas ang atong ginhawa, ang gas nga atong gibuga gikan sa lawas mao ang carbon dioxide!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes regeneration of an arm, which is not one of the three listed characteristics (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not teach growth in the sense of increasing size, nor response or reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: has five thin, wiggly arms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions arms as outer body parts but does not describe their role in movement or gathering food. It only states that arms can regrow, not their function.

copy.en:
Can a brittle star grow back a lost arm?

Yes! This starfish relative has five thin, wiggly arms, and if one breaks off, it can regrow a brand-new one.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang tumubo ulit ang braso ng brittle star?

Oo! Ang kamag-anak na ito ng starfish ay may limang manipis na braso, at kapag naputol ang isa, kaya nitong pumatubo ng bago.
copy.bis:
Makahimo ba og bag-ong bukton ang brittle star?

Oo! Kining paryente sa starfish adunay lima ka nipis nga bukton, ug kon maputol ang usa, makahimo kini og bag-o.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions copper, a metal used by local communities, but does not identify properties and uses of metals such as iron, gold, silver, and copper. It focuses on bronze as an alloy and its historical use, not on the properties and uses of the listed metals.

copy.en:
What makes bronze so tough?

Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. It's harder than pure copper, so ancient peoples used it to make tools and weapons!
copy.tl:
Bakit napakatigas ng bronze?

Ang bronze ay isang alloy na gawa sa tanso at lata. Mas matigas ito kaysa purong tanso, kaya ginamit ito ng mga sinaunang tao para sa kasangkapan at armas!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga lig-on kaayo ang bronze?

Ang bronze usa ka alloy sa tanso ug lata. Mas lig-on kini kaysa purong tanso, busa gigamit sa mga karaang tawo para sa mga himan ug hinagiban!

copy.en: Bryde's whale is a baleen whale that lives in the warm waters of the Philippines all year, eating small fish and krill by straining them from the water.
copy.tl: Ang Bryde's whale ay isang baleen na balyena na nakatira sa mainit na tubig ng Pilipinas sa buong taon, kumakain ng maliliit na isda at krill sa pamamagitan ng pagsala sa tubig.
copy.bis: Ang Bryde's whale usa ka baleen nga balyena nga nagpuyo sa init nga tubig sa Pilipinas sa tibuok tuig, nagkaon og gagmay nga isda ug krill pinaagi sa pagsala sa tubig.

copy.en: Stone and concrete have high thermal mass! They soak up heat all day, then slowly release it at night to keep rooms comfy.
copy.tl: Ang bato at concrete ay may mataas na thermal mass! Sumisipsip sila ng init buong araw, tapos dahan-dahang naglalabas sa gabi para komportable ang loob.
copy.bis: Ang bato ug konkreto adunay taas nga thermal mass! Nagsipsip sila og init tibuok adlaw, dayon hinay-hinay nagagawas sa gabii para komportable ang sulod.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots and leaves, but it does not identify their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only states growth direction, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A bulb has a flat base where roots grow downward, while leaves sprout upward from the top.
copy.tl: Ang bombilya ay may patag na bahagi sa ilalim kung saan tumutubo pababa ang mga ugat, at sa itaas naman tumutubo pataas ang mga dahon.
copy.bis: Ang bombilya adunay patag nga bahin sa ilalom diin motubo paubos ang mga gamot, ug sa ibabaw motubo pataas ang mga dahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bicol has more than one active volcano!

assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that Bicol has multiple active volcanoes and that ash may come from Mayon or Bulusan. It does not discuss patterns of eruptions over the last 100 years, nor does it assess or describe how predictable eruption patterns are. This is background knowledge about volcano locations, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why might families in Bicol see ash from different volcanoes?

Bicol has more than one active volcano! Families there may see ash from Mayon at some times, and from Bulusan at others.
copy.tl:
Bakit makakita ang mga pamilya sa Bicol ng ash mula sa iba't ibang bulkan?

May higit sa isang active volcano ang Bicol! Minsan makikita ng mga pamilya ang ash mula sa Mayon, at ibang pagkakataon mula sa Bulusan.
copy.bis:
Nganong makakita ang mga pamilya sa Bicol og ash gikan sa lainlaing bulkan?

Daghan pa’y active volcano sa Bicol! Usahay makakita ang pamilya og ash gikan sa Mayon, ug usahay gikan sa Bulusan.

copy.en: A Bunsen burner produces a hot flame by mixing flammable gas under pressure with controlled amounts of air, and it is used for heating substances.
copy.tl: Ang Bunsen burner ay gumagawa ng mainit na apoy sa pamamagitan ng paghahalo ng flammable gas sa ilalim ng pressure sa kontroladong dami ng hangin, at ginagamit ito para sa pag-init ng mga substance.
copy.bis: Ang Bunsen burner naghimo og init nga siga pinaagi sa pagsagol sa flammable gas ubos sa pressure sa kontrolado nga gidaghanon sa hangin, ug gigamit kini sa pagpainit sa mga substance.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the basic convection phenomenon (hot air rises, cool air sinks) but does not identify any advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, or radiation as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hot air is lighter and less dense than cool air! This difference makes the hot air rise and the cool air sink, causing air to circulate.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes density differences and circulation but does not explain convection in terms of the particle model (particle motion, spacing, energy transfer) as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hot air is lighter and less dense than cool air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air as a gas but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or their existence; it only uses the concept of density for air.

copy.en:
Why does hot air rise while cool air sinks in a room?

Hot air is lighter and less dense than cool air! This difference makes the hot air rise and the cool air sink, causing air to circulate.
copy.tl:
Bakit umaahon ang mainit na hangin habang bumababa ang malamig na hangin?

Mas magaan at mas mababa ang density ng mainit na hangin kaysa malamig! Kaya umaahon ang mainit at bumababa ang malamig, na nagpapaikot ng hangin.
copy.bis:
Nganong motaas ang mainit nga hangin samtang molubog ang bugnaw nga hangin?

Mas magaan ug mas ubos ang density sa mainit nga hangin kaysa bugnaw! Mao nga motaas ang mainit ug molubog ang bugnaw, nagpalibot sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water expands slightly and gets lighter when it freezes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions freezing but does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) and does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency. The focus is on density and floating, not on describing state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water expands slightly and gets lighter when it freezes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on freezing as a temperature-related change, but it does not describe how temperature causes matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It explains density and buoyancy instead, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why does ice float on water?

Water expands slightly and gets lighter when it freezes! This makes ice less dense, so it floats.
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang yelo sa tubig?

Bahagyang lumalaki at gumagaan ang tubig kapag namuo! Kaya mas mababa ang densidad ng yelo at lumulutang ito.
copy.bis:
Nganong magalutaw ang yelo sa tubig?

Molapad og gamay ug mogaan ang tubig kon mamuo! Busa mas ubos ang densidad sa yelo ug magalutaw kini.
